Northbridge University • Student Handbook Page 2

Welcome and University Overview

 Northbridge University is a fictional comprehensive university established for this demonstration dataset. The
 University offers undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs through schools and departments operating
 under common academic, student-support, and conduct standards.

 The Student Handbook explains the practical rules and services that shape student life. It should be read together
 with program specifications, course outlines, examination instructions, residence rules, information-technology
 policies, and any notices issued by authorized University offices.

 Students are expected to act with integrity, respect the rights of others, protect University property, comply with
 reasonable instructions, and maintain accurate contact information. Ignorance of a published rule does not normally
 exempt a student from its application.

 Student Rights and Responsibilities

 Students have the right to access teaching and learning resources appropriate to their enrolled program, receive
 published academic information, be treated with dignity, raise legitimate concerns without retaliation, and use
 established appeal and grievance channels.

 Students are responsible for attending required activities, meeting assessment deadlines, protecting confidential
 information, using digital systems lawfully, observing safety requirements, paying approved charges by due dates,
 and keeping their student record accurate.

 Where a conflict exists between a general handbook statement and a formally approved program or examination
 regulation,

ir student record accurate.

 Where a conflict exists between a general handbook statement and a formally approved program or examination
 regulation, the more specific approved regulation normally governs the academic matter. Students should seek
 written clarification from the relevant office when uncertain.

 Enrollment, Registration and Student Records

 Enrollment is confirmed after admission conditions are satisfied and registration is completed. Students must register
 within the published registration window unless an authorized late-registration process is available.

 Course changes, withdrawals, deferrals, leave requests, and program changes require the approvals specified by the
 relevant academic unit. Verbal permission from an instructor does not by itself change the official student record.

 Students must promptly report changes to their legal name, emergency contact,

m an instructor does not by itself change the official student record.

 Students must promptly report changes to their legal name, emergency contact, mailing address, phone number, or
 other required information. Official notices may be delivered through the University's student portal and institutional
 email.

 Attendance and Classroom Conduct

 Students should review the attendance requirement stated in each course outline. A course may have laboratory,
 clinical, studio, fieldwork, seminar, or participation requirements that differ from a standard lecture course.

 Students must not disrupt teaching, intimidate participants, record restricted activities without permission, or misuse
 classroom technology. Faculty may ask a student to leave a session when conduct materially interferes with
 instruction, subject to applicable procedures.

oom technology. Faculty may ask a student to leave a session when conduct materially interferes with
 instruction, subject to applicable procedures.

 Absence due to an emergency should be reported through the designated process as soon as reasonably possible.
 Supporting documentation may be requested where an accommodation or assessment adjustment is sought.

 Academic Integrity

 Academic integrity requires that submitted work accurately represent the student's own contribution and properly
 acknowledge sources and permitted assistance. Prohibited conduct may include plagiarism, fabrication, unauthorized
 collaboration, impersonation, contract cheating, falsification of records, and unauthorized access to assessment

Northbridge University • Student Handbook Page 3

materials.

 Use of generative AI or other automated tools is governed by the individual course's assessment instructions. Where
 a course permits such tools, students remain responsible for accuracy, attribution, privacy, and compliance with the
 stated conditions.

 Allegations of academic misconduct are handled through a defined process that may include notice of the concern, an
 opportunity to respond, review of evidence, a decision by an authorized officer or panel, and an appeal route where
 applicable.

 Student Wellbeing and Support Services

 The University maintains advising and support services covering academic advising, accessibility, counseling
 referrals, careers, financial guidance, student activities, and library support. Availability and operating hours may vary
 during examination and vacation periods.

rs, financial guidance, student activities, and library support. Availability and operating hours may vary
 during examination and vacation periods.

 Students seeking disability-related adjustments should contact the accessibility office early enough to allow
 documentation review and implementation. Adjustments are individualized and may not alter an essential learning
 outcome.

 Confidentiality is respected within the limits of applicable law, safeguarding duties, and institutional procedures.
 Students should use emergency services rather than routine University support channels for immediate threats to life
 or safety.

 Campus Safety, Security and Emergency Procedures

 Students must follow campus safety instructions, evacuation notices, laboratory rules, fire-safety requirements, and
 access controls. Doors, alarms, fire equipment,

ollow campus safety instructions, evacuation notices, laboratory rules, fire-safety requirements, and
 access controls. Doors, alarms, fire equipment, and emergency routes must not be obstructed or misused.

 Lost identification cards should be reported promptly. Access credentials are personal and must not be lent to another
 person. Security staff may verify identity when required for access or incident response.

 In an emergency, students should follow instructions from security personnel, emergency coordinators, or public
 emergency services. After an incident, official updates should be obtained from University communication channels
 rather than unverified social-media messages.

 Information Technology and Acceptable Use

 University accounts, networks, laboratories, and licensed software are provided primarily for academic and authorized
 administrative purposes.

Use

 University accounts, networks, laboratories, and licensed software are provided primarily for academic and authorized
 administrative purposes. Users must protect passwords, use multi-factor authentication where required, and promptly
 report suspected compromise.

 Prohibited activities include unauthorized access, distribution of malicious software, deliberate disruption of services,
 credential sharing, copyright infringement, and attempts to bypass security controls. Monitoring may occur for
 security, compliance, and service-management purposes in accordance with applicable rules.

 University-provided storage should not be treated as the sole copy of important personal work. Students should
 maintain appropriate backups and observe restrictions on storing sensitive information in shared systems.

should
 maintain appropriate backups and observe restrictions on storing sensitive information in shared systems.

 Student Organizations and Events

 Recognized student organizations may conduct activities subject to registration, safety, room-booking, financial, and
 conduct requirements. Organizations are responsible for the actions of their officers and for complying with event
 conditions.

 Events involving external speakers, large attendance, amplified sound, fundraising, travel, or unusual safety
 considerations may require advance approval. No organization may represent itself as an official University authority

unless authorized.

 Residence, Dining and Personal Property

 Where the University provides accommodation, residents must comply with residence rules concerning occupancy,
 visitors, quiet hours, cleanliness, prohibited items, fire safety, and damage reporting. Residence-specific rules may
 supplement this handbook.

 Students remain responsible for their personal property. The University does not ordinarily guarantee against loss or
 theft and may require residents to use approved storage or insurance arrangements.

 Fees, Financial Responsibility and Refunds

 Students are responsible for approved tuition, registration, examination, accommodation, laboratory, library, and other
 charges applicable to their enrollment. Payment deadlines are published in the fee schedule and student portal.

 Failure to pay by the deadline may result in restrictions on registration,

. Payment deadlines are published in the fee schedule and student portal.

 Failure to pay by the deadline may result in restrictions on registration, access to selected services, or release of
 certain documents, subject to applicable hardship and appeal procedures. Refunds, where available, are calculated
 under the fee policy rather than by informal arrangement.

 Complaints, Grievances and Appeals

 Students should normally raise concerns first with the office or person closest to the issue, unless the matter involves
 safety, harassment, discrimination, academic misconduct, or another issue for which a specialized route exists.

 Formal complaints should identify the issue, relevant dates, supporting documents, and the outcome sought. The
 University may decline to reopen a matter that has already received a final decision unless new evidence or a

documents, and the outcome sought. The
 University may decline to reopen a matter that has already received a final decision unless new evidence or a
 recognized procedural ground is presented.

 Disciplinary Process

 Non-academic misconduct may include harassment, threats, violence, theft, vandalism, serious disruption,
 unauthorized access, misuse of University property, or repeated breaches of published rules.

 Possible outcomes depend on the seriousness and circumstances of the matter and may include warning,
 educational measures, restitution, restrictions, suspension, or other sanctions authorized by University regulations.
 Procedural fairness includes notice and an opportunity to respond.

 Key Contacts and Student Checklist

 Students should save the official contact details shown in the current student portal for Academic Registry, Student
 Affairs, Finance, Examinations,

Students should save the official contact details shown in the current student portal for Academic Registry, Student
 Affairs, Finance, Examinations, Library, IT Helpdesk, Accessibility Services, Campus Security, and their school or
 department.

 Before each semester, students should confirm enrollment, review their timetable, check assessment dates, settle or
 arrange approved fee payments, verify contact information, and read notices from their school.

Northbridge University • Scholarship Policy Page 2

Purpose and Scope

 The Scholarship Policy establishes a transparent framework for merit, need-based, access, achievement, and named
 scholarship awards administered by the University. Individual scholarships may have additional donor or program
 conditions.

 Scholarships are normally applied to eligible University charges and do not automatically create a cash entitlement.
 The award letter states the amount, duration, eligible charges, renewal conditions, and any restrictions.

 Scholarship Categories

 Merit awards may consider academic performance and other published achievements. Need-based awards may
 consider household financial circumstances using information and evidence requested by the Financial Aid Office.

 Access and inclusion awards may be designed for students meeting defined participation or background criteria
 established by the relevant scheme.

 Eligibility

 Unless a scholarship notice states otherwise, applicants must be admitted or enrolled in an eligible program, satisfy
 the published application requirements, and remain in good academic and disciplinary standing.

admitted or enrolled in an eligible program, satisfy
 the published application requirements, and remain in good academic and disciplinary standing.

 Some awards require a minimum study load. Students who reduce their registered load, take approved leave, change
 programs, or receive another award must notify Financial Aid when required so that eligibility can be reassessed.

 Scholarships are not normally transferable between students. A student who is found ineligible after an award is made
 may have the award reduced, suspended, or withdrawn under the applicable procedure.

 Application and Evidence

 Applications should be submitted through the designated portal before the published deadline. Typical evidence may
 include academic records, fee information, household income documentation, personal statements, recommendation
 letters, or evidence of achievement.

include academic records, fee information, household income documentation, personal statements, recommendation
 letters, or evidence of achievement.

 Applicants are responsible for truthful and complete information. The University may verify documents and may
 request clarification or additional evidence. Missing evidence may affect eligibility if it prevents assessment against
 the published criteria.

 Selection and Review

 Scholarship decisions are made by the authorized committee or office identified in the scholarship announcement.
 Selection criteria should be applied consistently to the eligible applicant pool.

 Where a scholarship has limited funding, meeting the minimum criteria does not necessarily guarantee an award. The
 University may establish a reserve list and may reallocate unused funds according to the published scheme.

not necessarily guarantee an award. The

Award Amounts and Disbursement

 Award amounts are communicated in the award letter. Where the award is a percentage of tuition, the calculation is
 based on the eligible tuition charge defined by the scheme and may exclude optional services.

 Scholarship credits are normally posted after enrollment is confirmed and required conditions are met. If a student has
 an outstanding balance, the award may first be applied against eligible charges.

 Renewal and Academic Progress

 Renewable scholarships generally require continued enrollment, satisfactory academic progress, compliance with the
 award's minimum GPA or credit requirements, and good standing.

 A failed course, reduced load, leave of absence, or program change may trigger a review rather than an automatic
 cancellation. The review outcome depends on the scholarship's stated renewal rules and the student's circumstances.

review rather than an automatic
 cancellation. The review outcome depends on the scholarship's stated renewal rules and the student's circumstances.

 Other Funding and Double Funding

 Students must disclose other scholarships, sponsorships, tuition waivers, or grants when an award's rules require
 disclosure. Combined funding may be capped at eligible educational costs.

 Receiving external funding does not automatically cancel a University scholarship, but the University may adjust
 awards where required to prevent funding above eligible costs or where a donor agreement imposes restrictions.

 Appeals, Reconsideration and Fraud

 A student may request reconsideration where the scholarship rules provide an appeal route. Requests should identify
 the decision, the relevant rule, and the evidence supporting reconsideration.

 False statements, forged documents,

 False statements, forged documents, deliberate concealment of material information, or misuse of scholarship funds
 may result in withdrawal of the award and referral under applicable disciplinary or financial procedures.

 Examples and Frequently Asked Questions

 Example: A student receives a renewable tuition scholarship requiring a 3.00 GPA and 24 completed credits per
 academic year. If the student completes 21 credits, renewal is reviewed under the stated progress rules rather than
 assumed automatically.

 Example: A need-based applicant whose family income changes substantially after submission should report the
 change if the scheme requires continuing disclosure.

Northbridge University • Fee Policy Page 2

Purpose and Definitions

 The Fee Policy defines common student charges, payment deadlines, account controls, refunds, installment
 arrangements, and financial clearance. Program-specific schedules may contain additional charges approved through
 the University's fee-setting process.

 Tuition refers to the academic charge for registered study. Other charges may include registration, examination,
 laboratory, fieldwork, technology, accommodation, library replacement, or optional services.

 Billing and Payment Deadlines

 Student accounts are normally generated before the start of each semester. The statement identifies assessed
 charges, credits, prior balances, payment deadlines, and any installment schedule.

 Payment received after the deadline may be subject to a late charge or registration restriction. A student should not
 assume that an attempted payment has cleared until the account reflects the transaction.

 Installment Plans

 Eligible students may request an approved installment plan before the deadline stated by Finance. An installment plan
 does not waive charges; it changes the timing of payment.

 Failure to meet an installment date may cancel the arrangement and make the remaining balance immediately due,
 subject to the University's hardship and appeal procedures.

 Refunds and Withdrawal

 Refund eligibility depends on the date of official withdrawal and the type of charge. Administrative, application, or
 third-party charges may be non-refundable even when tuition is partially refundable.

Refund calculations use the University's official withdrawal date, not the date a student stops attending informally.
 Accommodation, visa, laboratory, and external charges may follow separate schedules.

 Financial Holds and Clearance

 An unpaid balance may place a financial hold on selected services. Depending on the amount and nature of the debt,
 the hold may restrict registration, transcript release, examination entry, accommodation renewal, or other services
 where permitted.

 Students who believe a charge is incorrect should contact Finance promptly with the student number, transaction
 date, receipt, and explanation. Disputing a charge does not automatically suspend the original due date.

 Sponsorships and Third-Party Payments

 Sponsored students must provide valid sponsorship documentation before the relevant billing deadline. The

.

 Sponsorships and Third-Party Payments

 Sponsored students must provide valid sponsorship documentation before the relevant billing deadline. The
 University may require the sponsor to confirm covered charges, duration, and payment procedure.

 Students remain responsible for charges not covered by the sponsor and for balances arising when a sponsor does
 not pay within the University's required timeframe.

 Waivers and Hardship Requests

 Fee waivers or extensions are exceptional and require documented grounds and approval by the authorized office. A
 waiver request should state the charge, reason, requested relief, supporting evidence, and proposed payment plan
 where relevant.

 Approval of an exception in one case does not establish a permanent entitlement or precedent for other students.

 Disputed Transactions and Refund Processing

 Electronic payment disputes should be reported with the payment reference and evidence of deduction. Duplicate
 payments may be applied to a future balance or refunded after verification.

 Approved refunds are normally returned through the payment method or bank details recorded in the student finance
 system. Processing time may vary because of bank and verification procedures.

 Financial Conduct and Frequently Asked Questions

 Students must not use another person's payment credentials without authorization, submit altered receipts, or attempt
 to manipulate billing records. Suspected fraudulent transactions may be investigated.

Northbridge University • Examination Rules Page 2

Purpose and Authority

 The Examination Rules establish requirements for quizzes, midterms, final examinations, practical assessments,
 online assessments, invigilation, misconduct, accommodations, results, and appeals.

 Course outlines may impose additional instructions provided they are consistent with approved academic regulations.
 Examination instructions issued by the Examinations Office on the day of an assessment are binding for that
 assessment.

 Examination Eligibility and Registration

 Students must be properly enrolled in the course and meet any prerequisite or attendance requirements stated in the
 applicable regulations. A student whose registration is not confirmed should contact the relevant academic office
 before the examination period.

 Examination timetables are published through official channels. Students are responsible for checking dates, times,
 venues,

the examination period.

 Examination timetables are published through official channels. Students are responsible for checking dates, times,
 venues, and permitted materials.

 Candidate Conduct

 Candidates must arrive before the reporting time, bring valid identification where required, follow seating instructions,
 and comply with invigilator directions.

 Unauthorized communication, possession or use of prohibited devices, copying, impersonation, access to concealed
 notes, or attempts to obtain unauthorized assistance may constitute examination misconduct.

 Permitted Materials and Devices

 Unless an examination paper explicitly permits an item, students should assume it is prohibited. Permitted calculators,
 reference sheets, dictionaries, or other materials will be specified in advance.

 Mobile phones, smart watches, wireless earbuds,

itted calculators,
 reference sheets, dictionaries, or other materials will be specified in advance.

 Mobile phones, smart watches, wireless earbuds, and other communication devices must be handled according to the
 examination instructions. A device being switched off does not automatically make it permitted in every assessment.

 Late Arrival, Early Departure and Absence

 Late arrival may be permitted only within the period stated by the Examinations Office and may not result in additional
 time. Once a candidate has received the paper, special restrictions may apply to entry.

 Students who miss an examination because of a documented emergency should submit a special-consideration
 request within the stated deadline. Approval may result in an alternative assessment, deferred examination, or
 another remedy defined by regulation.

roval may result in an alternative assessment, deferred examination, or

 Academic and Examination Misconduct

 Where misconduct is suspected, an invigilator may record the incident and preserve relevant evidence. The candidate
 may be allowed to continue the assessment unless the circumstances require removal for safety or integrity reasons.

 An allegation is not itself a final finding. The student receives the procedural opportunity specified by the academic
 integrity or examination misconduct rules, and outcomes are determined by the authorized decision-maker.

 Assessment Accommodations

 Approved accommodations may include additional time, accessible rooms, assistive technology, breaks, alternative
 formats, or other adjustments. Students should ensure that approved accommodations have been communicated to

sistive technology, breaks, alternative
 formats, or other adjustments. Students should ensure that approved accommodations have been communicated to
 the examination office before the assessment.

An accommodation does not excuse compliance with academic integrity requirements or permit materials not
 authorized under the accommodation plan.

 Marking, Results and Grade Changes

 Examinations are marked using the approved assessment criteria. Results are released through the official student
 information system after required checks.

 Grade changes require an authorized academic process. A grade should not be altered informally merely because a
 student requests a different result; corrections normally require evidence of an error or an approved academic
 decision.

 Rechecking, Review and Appeals

 Students may request a result review where regulations provide for it. The request should be made within the
 published window and should identify the relevant course, assessment, and grounds.

 A review may confirm the original mark, increase it, or,

hin the

 A review may confirm the original mark, increase it, or, where the regulations explicitly permit, identify an error
 requiring another outcome. Students should consult the applicable assessment regulation before submitting a
 request.

 Online and Remote Examinations

 Remote assessments may require identity verification, a stable connection, approved software, and a suitable
 examination environment. Students should complete any system check before the assessment.

 Technical problems should be reported through the designated channel as soon as possible, with screenshots,
 timestamps, and relevant error messages where feasible. A student should not deliberately disrupt a system and later
 claim a technical issue.

 Examination Day Checklist

 Before leaving for an examination, students should confirm the venue, reporting time, identification requirements,
 permitted materials, calculator rules, and any approved accommodation.

 During the examination, students should read the instructions carefully, write only in permitted areas, keep
 unauthorized devices stored as instructed, and raise procedural concerns with the invigilator rather than attempting to
 resolve them through communication with another candidate.

Northbridge University • Admission Guidelines Page 2

Admission Principles

 The Admission Guidelines describe the standard application journey for undergraduate and graduate applicants. They
 are designed for a fictional university knowledge base and illustrate the type of information an admissions assistant
 may retrieve.

 Admission decisions should be based on published eligibility criteria, complete documentation, program capacity, and
 any approved selection procedure. Individual programs may impose additional requirements.

 Undergraduate Eligibility

 Applicants should hold the required secondary-school or equivalent qualification for the intended program. Minimum
 grades, prerequisite subjects, and subject combinations are specified by each program.

 Some programs may require mathematics, laboratory sciences, language proficiency, portfolio evidence, aptitude
 testing, or an interview. Applicants should check the program-specific admissions page before applying.

 Graduate Eligibility

 Graduate applicants normally require a recognized bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant field. A

ying.

 Graduate Eligibility

 Graduate applicants normally require a recognized bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant field. A
 program may specify minimum academic standing, prerequisite courses, work experience, research interests, or a
 writing sample.

 Research-degree applicants may be asked to provide a research proposal, evidence of prior research, and potential
 supervisor information. A proposal does not guarantee supervisor availability or admission.

 Application Documents

 Typical documents include academic transcripts, certificates or degree documents, identification, photographs where
 required, personal statement, CV, recommendation letters, portfolio, test results, and proof of language proficiency
 where applicable.

 Documents not in an accepted language may require an authorized translation. The University may request originals

 or verified copies at enrollment.

 Application Fees and Waivers

 Where an application fee applies, the amount and payment deadline are shown in the application portal. Fee waivers
 may be available for categories identified in the current admissions notice.

Northbridge University • Admission Guidelines Page 3

An application is not considered complete merely because the fee has been paid. Required documents and
 declarations must also be submitted.

 Selection and Interviews

 Selection may involve academic review, scoring against published criteria, interview, test, portfolio assessment, or a
 combination. Not all applicants who meet minimum eligibility are necessarily admitted where capacity is limited.

 Interview invitations and decisions are communicated through official channels. Applicants should retain copies of
 submitted materials and correspondence.

 Offers and Conditions

 An offer may be unconditional or conditional. Conditions may include final examination results, document verification,
 language requirements, fee payment, or completion of another requirement.

 Applicants must satisfy all conditions by the stated deadline.

ification,
 language requirements, fee payment, or completion of another requirement.

 Applicants must satisfy all conditions by the stated deadline. Failure to satisfy a condition may result in withdrawal of
 the offer unless an extension is formally granted.

 Transfer, Credit and Advanced Standing

 Transfer applicants may request recognition of prior learning or credit. Recognition is determined by the academic unit
 based on content, level, learning outcomes, currency, and other approved criteria.

 Admission to a higher semester does not automatically mean every previous course will transfer. The official credit
 decision is recorded by the academic registry.

 International Applicants

 International applicants may need evidence of language proficiency, educational equivalence, financial capacity, and
 immigration documentation as applicable.

ional applicants may need evidence of language proficiency, educational equivalence, financial capacity, and
 immigration documentation as applicable. Visa or immigration decisions are made by the relevant government
 authority.

 Applicants should not rely on unofficial agents or social-media messages for immigration or admission requirements.
 Official University and government sources should be used for current instructions.

 Fraud, Misrepresentation and Application Changes

 Applicants must provide accurate information. Altered documents, false declarations, impersonation, or concealment
 of material facts may lead to rejection, withdrawal of an offer, cancellation of enrollment, or referral under applicable
 rules.

 Material changes after submission should be reported through the admissions portal or designated office. Applicants

ferral under applicable
 rules.

 Material changes after submission should be reported through the admissions portal or designated office. Applicants
 should not create multiple applications to circumvent a restriction unless instructed by Admissions.

 Appeals and Reconsideration

 Where an admission appeal or reconsideration route exists, the applicant must submit the request within the stated
 deadline and identify the specific basis for review. Appeals do not guarantee a change in decision.

Calendar Overview

 The 2026–2027 academic calendar provides a planning framework for teaching, registration, examinations, breaks,
 results, and major administrative deadlines. Program-level calendars may differ where professional, clinical,
 laboratory, or cohort requirements apply.

 Students should verify dates in the official portal before making travel, accommodation, employment, or examination
 plans. Dates may be revised by authorized University notice.

Registration Windows

 Registration normally opens before classes and may include separate windows for continuing students, new students,
 late registration, and program-specific cohorts.

 Students who miss registration should contact their academic registry immediately. Late registration may require
 approval and may carry an administrative charge where authorized.

 Assessment and Examination Milestones

 Course outlines should identify major assessment dates. Central examination timetables are normally published
 before the examination period. Students should report timetable conflicts through the designated process before the
 stated deadline.

 Special consideration, deferred assessment, and examination appeals may have deadlines that differ from ordinary
 academic calendar dates.

 Graduation and Degree Clearance

 Students approaching graduation should review degree requirements, outstanding fees, library obligations, and any
 required applications. Graduation application deadlines are published separately where cohorts or ceremonies require
 different processing.

 Completion of classes does not automatically mean degree clearance. Academic Registry confirms completion after
 grades and other requirements are finalized.

 Academic Advising and Planning

 Advising periods are intended to help students review progression, prerequisites, course choices, graduation
 planning, and academic risks. Students remain responsible for checking their official degree audit and registration.

 Calendar Change Procedure

 Changes to major dates require authorization by the relevant University authority. Updated calendars should show an
 effective date or revision notice where practicable.

 Where a change affects an examination or assessment, the University should communicate the revised date through
 official channels. Students should keep evidence of approved individual arrangements.
